original_question: It is known that the group Zω has a subgroup whose dual is free abelian of rank 2ℵ0(see 17.24 in Archive). Does Zω have a subgroup whose dual is free ℵ0 abelian of still larger rank(the largest possible being 22)? This is Question 11 in(G. M. Bergman, Portugaliae Math., 69(2012) 69–84).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.13 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", with archived Problem 17.24 as the explicit background result it builds on.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the ambient group Z^ω, the known benchmark result that some subgroup has dual free abelian of rank 2^{aleph_0}, the fact that the dual is required to be free abelian, and the intended follow-up question asking whether a strictly larger rank can occur. It also correctly points to archived Problem 17.24 and to Bergman's 2012 paper.
missing_details: Make the quantified object explicit: the question asks whether there exists a subgroup G <= Z^ω with the stated property.
Spell out that Z^ω means the countable direct product of copies of Z, not the direct sum.
Define "dual" explicitly as the algebraic dual Hom(G, Z), to avoid confusion with any topological dual.
Clarify that "still larger rank" means strictly larger than 2^{aleph_0}, since Problem 17.24 already supplies rank 2^{aleph_0}.
Correct the garbled maximal-cardinality notation: the upper bound mentioned is 2^{2^{aleph_0}}.
State explicitly that the dual is required to be a free abelian group of that rank.
refined_question: Since a subgroup of Z^ω is known to have algebraic dual of free abelian rank 2^{aleph_0}, does there exist a subgroup G <= Z^ω, where Z^ω is the countable direct product of copies of Z, such that Hom(G, Z) is a free abelian group of rank strictly larger than 2^{aleph_0}; more specifically, can one achieve rank 2^{2^{aleph_0}}?
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Problem 21.13 itself, apart from typographical corruption in the cardinal notation. That problem explicitly cites archived Problem 17.24 as the known starting point, namely that Z^ω does have a subgroup with free dual of rank 2^{aleph_0}, and then asks for a larger possible rank. No nearby entry in the notebook is closer to the draft than 21.13, and the notebook does not supply a further equivalent reformulation there; so the faithful refinement is to keep the question narrowly about subgroups of Z^ω and make the implicit notation and quantifiers explicit.
